title: New dissector to support VITA49.2 context, extension context, command, and extension command packets
description:
- Support dissection of VITA49.2 context, extension context, command and extension command packets
- Allow customization of dissector to support specification derived from standard.

*This merge conflicts with approach used in commit c34223ad6219d2baffefbc05c72cffa3946988bb*

This is an impressive change in terms of user configuration of VITA 49 context packages. However, this merge request introduces a regression from the current behavior of Wireshark on the master with respect to VITA 49.

Loading the PCAP file from issue #18445 (vrt_sample_catpure_context_port_4991.pcap) with nightly wireshark-4.1.0rc0-2984-gc57fde44ade3 (correct):
![nightly](/uploads/adfea0ece4c6aab34498465abfb9a698/nightly.png)

Loading this same PCAP file with this branch (broken):
![this_merge_request](/uploads/6a6de5c7121b4e5668ae053dba94afa3/this_merge_request.png)

Everything after the "Context Association List" is broken by this merge request. The message "Dissector cannot parse the actual lists. Any subsequent fields will be wrong." warns that this is happening. But even with this warning, it is a bug/regression from current Wireshark. Wireshark already correctly parses the "Context Association List" and subsequent fields as seen above in the nightly.

Yes. This is one of the divergences from the approach used in commit listed at the top. Context Association List messages are variable size and use a unique format to specify the size which does not readily map into the description format. If that field is stripped the rest of the example pcap will parse correctly. It appeared the pcap was artificially created rather than an actual capture, so the open question for me was do context association list messages appear in the wild? There are likewise fields which are supported in this version but not the previous commit and fields supported in neither. It is regrettable that parallel development occurred, but the larger question at this point is what approach should be used to merge the two paths. The pertinent subquestion here being is it acceptable to drop behavior which may be extraneous in actual use?

> This is one of the divergences from the approach used in commit listed at the top.

I did fast review at the code in this merge request. This merge request removes many (all?) commits since 2021, not just the one commit above. Maybe you copied your modified old source over the master source instead of merging with git? The comments in packet-vrt.c have weird changes. And other examples (might be more):
1. removes RTP support (another regression): https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10103
2. removes CIF1 (might cause more regression): https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9620
3. removes cleanup by @martin.r.mathieson: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4520

> open question for me was do context association list messages appear in the wild?

Yes. Example use:
https://github.com/RedhawkSDR/VITA49/blob/master/doc/doxygen_html/classvrt_1_1ContextAssocLists.html#L60

> It is regrettable that parallel development occurred, but the larger question at this point is what approach should be used to merge the two paths. The pertinent subquestion here being is it acceptable to drop behavior which may be extraneous in actual use?

The Wireshark already supports the VITA 49 use cases for context association lists and RTP. In the perfect world, these use cases should not get broken by your XML change. It is unknown who is broken until they upgrades where their use case breaks. And only then do they open an issue which could take a lot of time. Core developers opinion?

It is possible I made a git blunder, but number 2 & number 3 don't apply to the code in this merge. number 1 appears to have been added after this merge branch was started; it should be added here.
I understand removing capability can have unexpected negative impact for public projects where we don't know to what extend feature may be used. With the redhawk example you provide, it is reasonable to consider the context lists a required feature. 
So the path I propose is, integrate packet-vrt to use the explicit approach added to master in the stated merge if no configuration file is defined (which will provide compatibility with any existing use, including context association lists, but partial support for CIF1 and no support for CIF2-3, command packets, or extension packets) and the configured approach from this merge if a file is defined (which won't support context association lists). This introduces some redundancy in the overlapping functionality which may make maintenance more difficult, but tighter integration of the approaches seems excessively difficult.
I merged the approaches selectable by a new preference flag (since the configuration file name is a preference of the sub-dissector).

Great, thank you. I will give this new version a try. I agree that selecting the XML behavior is the best solution from a usability and regression perspective. That way, the dissector will "just work" for average Wireshark users dissecting VITA49 and experts can load XML. XML config loading is not part of the typical Wireshark dissection workflow so not having to do it by default is best in my opinion.

This pcap extends on the previous example, removing the cifs not supported by the XML configuration but adding the additional cifs and packet types. You should be able to toggle the new configuration flag to observe the differences. Like the previous example, this is a constructed file rather than an actual capture, so the field values may not be realistic. [vrt-cif-standard-long-example.pcapng](/uploads/4bc40e9176ce4518155aeb0be42bf771/vrt-cif-standard-long-example.pcapng)

Thank you for that example pcapng file. I like the way Wireshare behaves much more than before since it does not break context association lists by leaving the old support with new XML optional.

A few more feedbacks:
1. In Edit, Preferences, Protocols, confusing for "VITA 49" and "V49 CIF" to each hold settings. When I wanted to changing the XML file, took a long time to find. Could the settings in "V49 CIF" be moved to "VITA 49"? If not, could you make them a leaf of a tree like the "29West"? Finally, if neither of those two options can work, I think rename "V49 CIF" to "VITA 49 CIF" to make adjacent in the GUI when sorted.
2. There are lots of spelling mistakes in the XML file. You might want to use a editor with a spell checker. No spelling errors helps for non-native English users when translating. I will mark a few mistakes to show.
3. Style - units are not consistent like both "fs" and "femto-seconds" in XML.
I have moved the VITA 49 CIF preferences to a subtree under VITA 49

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+# Quickstart
+1. Copy the configuration files to a convenient location
+2. Run wireshark and update the preferences
+   - Select Edit->Preferences...
+   - Select Protocols->VITA 49
+   - Uncheck "Use Ettus" and "Limit dissection"; set port number list (4991 typical). You can enter multiple ports separated by commas, and/or ranges with a dash.
+   - Select Protocols->V49 CIF
+   - Set filename to location of top configuration file; Check "Fallback" to enable default class id.
+3. Load example capture file. A sample pcap file is provided to verify the installation. This is a constructed file intended to highlight some of the parsing features and may not illustrate meaningful traffic at the system level.
+4. For live captures, apply a display filter to limit display (e.g., "vrt" for only VITA 49 packet)
+
+ ## Note on example file
+ The example file may have been created from a raw byte sequence. You can load the byte sequence directly with the "File->Import from Hex Dump..." menu item. Select the UDP radio button and indicate a port you have designated for V49 (e.g., 4992). The dump file will contain comments on the expected results.
+
+# Key Features added with this dissector
+## Changes to VITA 49 Protocol (packet-vrt):
+
+* Added preference "Limit dissection to VITA 49.0 format"
+   If enabled, the dissector should behave primarily as it did before with no extra interpretation of
+   new V49.2 fields.
+
+* Added parsing of new header fields as defiend by V49.2
+
+* Added link to new dissector for context and command packets
+
+## New V49 CIF Protocol (packet-vrt-cif):
+* Parse and display payload of context, extended context, control, and extended control packets
+
+* Preference "CIF description filename" set the top XML file to describe field parsing
+   - vrt-cif-standard-top.xml :   Top level for public field parsing only
+   - vrt-cif-warnerr.xml :        Common definitions of the warn/err bits (included from top)
+   - vrt-cif-standard.xml :       Description of fields described in V49.2 section 9 (included from top)
+   - vrt-cif-*project*.xml :      Description of extension fields defined for project (included from top)
+
+   VRT is not a specification, but a framework within which a specifications can be defined. It may be useful to refine the dissector to display only information from the standard which falls within the subset used by the system under test and flag variations. Since there are a large number of valid variations, this selection is not suited to a set of simple configuration properties. The dissector supports the customization by allowing the user to edit vrt-cif-standard.xml to describe their specific use of the standard. Similarly, the extended context/command packets are completely user specific, but if they are formatted in a similar fashion to the standard context/command packets as recommended by the standard, they can be described and parsed by the dissector with an additional xml file.
+
+* Preference "Fallback to default configuration" allows the default (no class id) configuration
+   to be used when a class id is provided but does not match one(s) defined.
+
